review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, self-review; not independent approval
review.decision: Separate verified current frontend authority from explicitly historical display/read-only association; close managed-launch presentation config gap and validate actual protocol semantics
review.notes: User asks to fix repeated native/tmux duplicate. Installed175/current primary407B JSON is the same corrupt record seen yesterday; current native row has exact scoped SID while tmux row lacks identity. Old exact frontend binding independently names still-live terminal client, but backend and frontend receipts changed; it must not become command authority. Existing1845 was read recovery only and not deployed, radar unchanged. No actual state repair, restores, input, queue replay/deletion, service restart, installation or release. HQ user manual restart is not automatic recovery; startup notification override is a proven adapter eligibility gap. Original terminal disconnect and corruption writer are not yet established and must remain unknown rather than blamed on quota/memory. Strict unique private evidence and incarnation checks, truthful pending/last-known semantics, guest fencing and no effective privilege escalation reviewed before any test/source implementation. Generated local schema is contract evidence, not real device/runtime acceptance. All fixtures/builds/raw in task temp; shared dirty root and old retained/refused resources protected. Scope changes require a new reviewed seal before changed assertions.

cases.description: Managed Codex presentation options keep the frontend adapter
cases.setup: Synthetic argv and the actual HQ launch recipe; no process or configuration mutations.
cases.action: Admit plain HQ argv and presentation-only tui.notifications in separated/inline config forms; attempt provider/home/endpoint/permissions/profile and malformed or mixed config values.
cases.expected: Only a narrowly parsed display-only notification override is newly admitted. Arguments remain byte-for-byte unchanged at launch; provider/home/remote/profile/headless/unknown configuration remains native. Help admission consumes config values and still sees later subcommands. No permission, auth, proxy or user configuration change.

cases.description: Root identity follows protocol semantics rather than analytics labels
cases.setup: Observer with independently verified same home and synthetic own request/response frames; generated installed Codex0.167.2 schema documents threadSource as analytics string.
cases.action: Send start/resume/fork with analytics labels, then ephemeral/helper/subagent/foreign-home/failure/unknown provenance/unmatched and out-of-order responses.
cases.expected: A successful own non-ephemeral root operation from cli/vscode can bind despite analytics label. Response provenance and parent/ephemeral facts remain decisive. Global notifications, arbitrary reads/catalogs, subagent parents, errors, foreign home, old responses and missing provenance never bind. Keep bounded pending/observation limits and source payload forwarding unchanged.

cases.description: Independent last-known conversation evidence is a display-only relation
cases.setup: Isolated private native binding receipt and exact-home terminal-origin native record, deterministic live Codex client/pane process witnesses and process births; primary absent/corrupt or expired same-session.
cases.action: Resolve historical relation, then vary PID incarnation, pane root, TTY, ambiguity, home, valid incumbent owner, receipt permissions/type/size and unknown/future timestamps.
cases.expected: Return last-known history only for one independently recorded relation whose exact terminal process and pane incarnation still match. Never parse a corrupt JSON prefix, infer by title/cwd/shared backend PID or change disk. A changed valid incumbent, missing/unsafe/ambiguous proof or PID/pane reuse fails closed. New live backend identity may differ only because this relation is explicitly historical; it never yields LoadLive, input, restore, HQ or lifecycle authority.

cases.description: Radar represents one conversation without fabricating live identity
cases.setup: Production native/tmux assembly with synthetic independent receipt and process probes; include same-directory and same-daemon unrelated threads, multiple homes and a verified newer conversation.
cases.action: Gather a pane plus the native copy, then remove/change/ambiguate the observation; check source records before/after.
cases.expected: Only the independently established unique last-known relation folds the native history into its pane presentation. Expose explicit association-pending/read-only history metadata; do not fill the authoritative session ID, change lifecycle status, grant input or prune the native observation. Genuine external clients and other threads remain. Existing verified identity takes precedence; absent evidence retains honest separate unknown data. Both projection and parser preserve no-write read semantics for this new fallback.

cases.description: Owner can view last-known history while guest and inputs stay fenced
cases.setup: Actual app pane reader and server endpoints with synthetic history and independent relation, scoped owner/guest requests; no real TTY or history.
cases.action: Read association-failed pane as owner and guest, use recent/history/304 cursors, switch association to a new verified thread and attempt existing input admission.
cases.expected: Owner may explicitly see last-known history with an unconfirmed/read-only response state and no false current-session assertion. Guest cannot take this fallback or receive candidate identifiers/content; deny before its history reader. Input and restore continue requiring original strict current evidence. ETag/cursors include identity/state; old headers cannot falsely persist after verification. Normal valid-empty/errors/recovered behavior remains.

cases.description: RN history state is visible and cannot enable sending
cases.setup: Mounted actual API/Detail/HQ/shared ChatView with isolated responses and existing send spies; no device or actual user conversation.
cases.action: Load unconfirmed last-known history, refresh304, switch pane while old request returns, then establish verified history.
cases.expected: Show bilingual last-known/read-only guidance, preserve visible turns, disable relevant chat send controls while this state applies and restore normal verified behavior afterward. Keep identity-scoped late-result guards and unchanged-poll memo behavior. No automatic resend, rebind or restore.

cases.description: Browser focused and tile views keep explicit read-only identity state
cases.setup: Actual browser handlers in isolated VM/synthetic server with unconfirmed/recovered/verified/guest and stale-target responses.
cases.action: Render focused and tile chats and row metadata, attempt send with unconfirmed state, refresh304 and change targets.
cases.expected: One server conversation projection stays one row; association-pending and last-known-history labels are consistent and never described as confirmed external ownership. Unconfirmed history is visibly read-only and cannot dispatch send. Verified recovery removes the restriction; stale responses cannot affect a new target. Normal external and existing owner/guest boundaries stay unchanged.

cases.description: Mac menu reflects pending association without duplicating server records
cases.setup: Actual Swift decoding and row-description helpers using synthetic agent JSON, no App/TCC/window interaction.
cases.action: Decode ordinary verified and last-known/read-only observations and render their status descriptions.
cases.expected: A missing verified session ID stays missing. Pending relation is labeled as such, distinct from confirmed external placement, and source row keys/targets retain existing meaning. No focus, input, installation or real screenshot is performed.
